question.text: Which of the following best describes the key difference between futures and options contracts?

answer.text: Futures create obligations for both parties, while options give the buyer a right but not an obligation
Futures are traded on exchanges while options are traded only OTC
Options require margin payments while futures do not
Futures have unlimited profit potential while options do not

explanation.text: The Logic: Futures contracts impose rights and obligations on both buyer and seller, whereas an option gives the buyer a right (without obligation) while the seller carries the obligation if exercised. That asymmetry is the defining contrast. The Trap: Saying "options do not require margin" is wrong - the workbook describes margining for portfolios containing both options and futures, and option extreme loss margin on open short option positions. Option buyers risk the premium paid, but option sellers and cleared exchange positions may be margined. Note: Anchor on the right-versus-obligation axis: that is what distinguishes futures from options, not the venue, the existence of margin, or the profit profile.
